findings.issue_text: [BUG] organization_auditlogs.py: organization_context is never defined in get(), so requests with optimized_pagination=true raise NameError and return a 500

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset branch uses queryset[start_offset:...] with negative indices, which Django ORM rejects with ValueError, causing a 500 when advanced features and negative-offset cursor are used
[BUG] paginate() has a fixed signature and does not forward **kwargs, so passing enable_advanced_features=True raises TypeError: unexpected keyword argument
[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key relies on self._is_asc which is only defined on datetime paginator subclasses, causing AttributeError
[BUG] get_item_key's int(math.floor(value)) assumes a numeric field but the endpoint orders by -datetime, raising TypeError: type datetime doesn't define __floor__

[ADVISORY] DateTimePaginator start_offset = max(0, offset) change is dead/no-op code; cursors are only constructed with non-negative offsets, so the negative-offset branch never triggers here and misleads future maintainers
[ADVISORY] The optimized_pagination behavior is gated on a raw query string with no feature flag or kill switch, so it cannot be disabled in production without a code deploy

[BUG] `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `cursor.offset` (parsed from client-supplied cursor via `int(offset)`), raising `ValueError` from Django ORM which rejects negative slice bounds since 1.6 — hard 500 on fully client-controlled input; the 'advanced feature' can never work

[BUG] In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the prev-cursor branch uses `start_offset = offset` unclamped, so a prev cursor with a negative offset (arbitrary client input) drives `queryset[negative:stop]` → `ValueError`, making the crash reachable on every paginated endpoint; the `max(0, offset)` clamp is only applied to the non-prev branch, leaving prev-path negative offsets unguarded and untested

[BUG] `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `self._is_asc(for_prev)` and `get_result` passes `self.desc` to `build_cursor`, but both attributes are defined only on concrete subclasses like `DateTimePaginator`, not `BasePaginator`, so `OptimizedCursorPaginator` raises `AttributeError: '_is_asc'` on its first successful query — the new code path can only ever return 500s

[BUG] In the prev-cursor dedup branch, `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: results = results[:-1]` compares against `offset` but results were sliced from `start_offset`, so when they differ the trailing element is never trimmed, returning `limit + 1` rows and off-by-one next-cursor math — duplicate row appears at a page boundary

[BUG] `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None check; for requests where the member context is absent (e.g. superuser not a member of the org), this raises `AttributeError` and returns 500 on the audit-log GET for users who previously received a 200

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap: the entire new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class (~95 lines including novel negative-offset logic) and modified `BasePaginator.get_result` slicing ship with zero tests in this diff; the shared `BasePaginator` regression silently affects every paginated endpoint and pre-existing tests never exercise negative or prev-with-negative offsets

[ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated on a raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` with no feature flag or way to disable short of a code deploy, and it silently changes the pagination contract — cursor semantics differ between `DateTimePaginator` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, so operators cannot turn the broken path off during an incident and cursor drift between paths produces skipped/duplicated rows

[ADVISORY] Dead/vestigial design: since the negative-offset branch crashes immediately, the entire 'negative offset support' rationale for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is infeasible in the Django ORM, meaning ~60 lines including the endpoint branch and `enable_advanced_features` plumbing fail the deletion test — maintainers inherit a second parallel paginator code path that adds no reachable optimization

[BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:70-77 — optimized_pagination branch references organization_context.member.has_global_access but organization_context is never defined in get(), causing NameError and 500 for every request with optimized_pagination=true

[BUG] paginator.py:838-852 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset < 0, raising Django's AssertionError 'Negative indexing is not supported'; negative-offset cursors cause 500s and the feature cannot execute

[BUG] paginator.py:179-185 — base paginator slicing logic changed for all DateTimePaginator/offset-based endpoints, silently clamping negative offsets to 0 and returning wrong-page results, an untraced behavior change to every paginated endpoint

[ADVISORY] organization_auditlogs.py:69-70 — new undocumented public query parameter optimized_pagination=true gated on is_superuser or has_global_access with no feature flag, API doc update, or options entry; API surface and authorization distinction operators cannot discover or disable without a deploy

[ADVISORY] paginator.py:842-856 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates ~40 lines of base get_result and the trim condition compares against original offset instead of start_offset, so fixes must be applied twice or will be missed

[ADVISORY] paginator.py:815-912 — OptimizedCursorPaginator is a new ~100-line class with non-trivial boundary logic and no tests in the diff; regressions would silently return wrong pages to superusers
[ADVISORY] cursors.py:26-27 — two-line comment claims 'performance optimization: allow negative offsets' that the code does not implement; misleading comment asserts unsupported Cursor invariant

[ADVISORY] paginator.py:815-830 — OptimizedCursorPaginator is speculative generality: its only functional delta over OffsetPaginator is the negative-offset branch that crashes; the class, enable_advanced_features flag, and optimized_pagination param exist to serve a feature that cannot work

[BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:74 references undefined `organization_context` in `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, causing NameError and 500 for all non-superuser requests on the audit log listing route

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to a datetime key attribute (order_by='-datetime'), raising TypeError since the datetime-to-int conversion present in DateTimePaginator is omitted

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator advanced branch slices queryset with a negative start_offset; Django explicitly rejects negative indices with AssertionError/ValueError, so negative-offset cursors cause a 500 instead of bidirectional pagination

[BUG] OffsetPaginator.get_result sets start_offset = offset for prev-cursors, allowing an unvalidated negative cursor offset to be used as a lower slice bound, causing Django negative-indexing errors on every OffsetPaginator-based endpoint

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a ~50-line near-verbatim copy of OffsetPaginator.get_result with only the slicing branch differing; the copies already diverge so future fixes to prev-cursor dedup logic won't apply to the audit-log path — the subclass should be deleted and the working delta merged into the base class

[ADVISORY] Behavior is branched on a raw, undocumented query param `optimized_pagination=true` with no feature flag or options entry, so operators cannot disable or roll out the paginator without a deploy, and toggling the param mid-traversal feeds cursors between paginators with different key encodings, producing wrong or empty pages

[ADVISORY] Comment in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py claims negative offsets enable efficient reverse pagination, but the code doesn't implement any negative-offset support; misleading comments at every layer describe a mechanism that doesn't exist

[BUG] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-183 — PR silently modifies shared BasePaginator.get_result offset-slicing logic used by every paginator, changing behavior of all offset-based cursor endpoints under a PR whose stated intent was only audit-log performance; unreviewed global pagination contract change

[BUG] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:879-884 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices queryset with start_offset < 0, raising Django ValueError 'Negative indexing is not supported'; since cursor.offset is client-controlled, a negative-offset cursor with optimized_pagination=true causes a 500 on the audit-logs endpoint

[BUG] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:889-891 — elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra uses raw negative offset in the prev-cursor dedup comparison while results were sliced from start_offset, so boundary-result trimming never fires when offset < 0, returning duplicate/incorrect rows on reverse pagination

[BUG] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-29 — Comment on Cursor.__init__ documents negative offsets as intentional, but the class-level contract of all existing paginators assumes offset >= 0; existing endpoints that previously raised on malformed negative cursors now flow into get_item_key/build_cursor paths never validated for negatives, causing silent behavior drift in unrelated endpoints

[ADVISORY] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:69-88 — Same endpoint returns two structurally different pagination behaviors selected by an undocumented raw query param plus a permission attribute, with no feature flag, API version, or migration path; response contract forks on user identity rather than client choice, with no way to disable without a deploy

[BUG] src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:72 — organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access') for non-superuser external actors where member is None, causing a 500 on the audit-log listing

[ADVISORY] src/sentry/api/paginator.py:818-908 — OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates ~60 lines of BasePaginator.get_result with drift already present; future fixes to BasePaginator will not propagate to the admin path, diverging audit-log admin UX from other paginated endpoints

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.offset < 0, and Django's QuerySet raises 'AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported' on any slice with a negative start; the code comment claims Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically, which is false, causing an unhandled 500 on the audit-log endpoint for any admin using optimized_pagination=true with a crafted negative-offset cursor

[BUG] The rewrite 'start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset' changes behavior for is_prev cursors on the default path: a prev-cursor with negative offset flows straight into queryset[offset:stop] and raises the same AssertionError; this regression is not gated behind optimized_pagination=true or a superuser check, and since cursors are unsigned base64 JSON, any client can trigger a 500 on all endpoints using DateTimePaginator-family get_result

[ADVISORY] The new pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter optimized_pagination plus an in-code superuser/global-access check with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled or rolled back without a code deploy

[ADVISORY] The enable_advanced check dereferences organization_context.member on a control-silo endpoint where that attribute's availability depends on the request path; if organization_context.member raises AttributeError for memberless contexts, the entire audit log endpoint would 500 for users who previously got results, and this client-controlled trigger runs on a code path whose assumption (member always present) is unverified

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is an untested hand-copied clone of OffsetPaginator.get_result with divergences (e.g. trimming uses offset while slice used start_offset, and cursor_value = 0 fallback instead of max(0, cursor.value)) that will only surface as wrong pages/500s in production

[ADVISORY] New negative-offset slicing in DateTimePaginator.get_result breaks the start_offset >= 0 invariant with no test update, allowing crafted cursors to cause 500s instead of 4xx via Django's ValueError on negative indexing

[ADVISORY] New dual-paginate branch in organization_auditlogs.py (optimized_pagination=true with is_superuser or has_global_access) has no endpoint test, leaving all four param × privilege combinations unverified and regressions invisible to CI

[BUG] In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result negative-offset branch, queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset raises Django's AssertionError 'Negative indexing is not supported', crashing the advanced feature path with a 500; the docstring claim that Django ORM handles negative slicing is false since negative slicing only works on materialized lists

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), which raises TypeError when the value is a datetime (as with the audit-log's -datetime order key), crashing every request using optimized_pagination=true on this endpoint

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result sets cursor.value=0 when cursor is None, causing build_queryset(0,...) to filter datetime <= 0 (epoch) and silently return zero rows instead of the first page

[BUG] BasePaginator.get_result keeps the raw negative offset on the prev path (start_offset = offset if cursor.is_prev), allowing a crafted prev-cursor with negative offset to reach queryset[negative:stop] and raise the 'Negative indexing is not supported' error, a remote-triggerable 500 on the default path

[ADVISORY] The prev-dedup fallback 'elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra' compares against the original offset even when the negative-offset branch computed a different start_offset, causing the dedup check to fire on wrong arithmetic and silently drop or duplicate rows on prev pages

[ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated only on a raw query parameter (optimized_pagination=true) combined with superuser/global-access checks, with no feature flag or option to disable it without a code deploy

[BUG] organization_context is referenced but never defined or imported in get() of organization_auditlogs.py, causing NameError (or misclassification of access) and a 500 on every request that reaches line 73
[BUG] `math.floor` on a datetime in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key raises TypeError, returning a 500 on every optimized request for the audit-log endpoint ordered by `-datetime`

[BUG] Negative-offset slicing in the paginator raises Django's `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`, producing a 500 instead of efficient bidirectional pagination (sites: paginator.py:876-882 and paginator.py:184-186)

[BUG] Clamping forward-cursor negative offsets to 0 in `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently returns the wrong page as a 200, and the subsequent `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check uses the unclamped offset so boundary correction can never match

[ADVISORY] The new paginator behavior is gated on a raw query param with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled without a code deploy; operators have no kill switch and the two paginators produce different cursor formats for the same endpoint depending on caller permissions
[ADVISORY] The new paginator's core behaviors (datetime key handling, negative-offset branch, prev-cursor trimming) have zero test coverage in this diff

[ADVISORY] Prev-cursor result trimming is dead/incorrect under the new offset regime: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: results = results[:-1]` compares against the unclamped offset while results were sliced from `start_offset`, so the trim either never fires or fires on the wrong page shape, leaving a duplicated boundary row when paging backwards

There is no feature flag, settings knob, or runtime kill switch shown to disable the optimized paginator in production without a deploy, so the advisory is diff-grounded and actionable but not inherently a correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `cursor.offset` (parsed from client-supplied cursor via `int(offset)`), raising `ValueError` from Django ORM which rejects negative slice bounds since 1.6 — hard 500 on fully client-controlled input; the 'advanced feature' can never work

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an explicit path that slices a Django queryset with a negative start index: in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and does `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The cursor offset is parsed via `Cursor.offset = int(offset)` (client-controlled cursor input). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so a negative `start_offset` can raise an exception (500) on client-controlled input, making the "advanced feature" unsafe/broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the prev-cursor branch uses `start_offset = offset` unclamped, so a prev cursor with a negative offset (arbitrary client input) drives `queryset[negative:stop]` → `ValueError`, making the crash reachable on every paginated endpoint; the `max(0, offset)` clamp is only applied to the non-prev branch, leaving prev-path negative offsets unguarded and untested

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` `BasePaginator.get_result` was changed to compute `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` and then slice `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. This leaves the `cursor.is_prev` path using an unclamped `offset`, so a negative `cursor.offset` will produce a negative queryset slice. The diff also shows `Cursor.offset` is set via `int(offset)` with no validation in `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py`, making negative offsets possible from cursor input. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices, so this can raise at runtime on the prev path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `self._is_asc(for_prev)` and `get_result` passes `self.desc` to `build_cursor`, but both attributes are defined only on concrete subclasses like `DateTimePaginator`, not `BasePaginator`, so `OptimizedCursorPaginator` raises `AttributeError: '_is_asc'` on its first successful query — the new code path can only ever return 500s

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator` inherits from `BasePaginator` and calls `super().__init__`, but it does not show the definition of `BasePaginator` (or `DateTimePaginator`) to verify whether `_is_asc` and `desc` are absent there. The finding asserts these attributes exist only on concrete subclasses, but that is not demonstrated by the provided diff; they may be implemented on `BasePaginator` in unchanged code, as is common for shared cursor-pagination helpers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the prev-cursor dedup branch, `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: results = results[:-1]` compares against `offset` but results were sliced from `start_offset`, so when they differ the trailing element is never trimmed, returning `limit + 1` rows and off-by-one next-cursor math — duplicate row appears at a page boundary

adjudication.rationale: In both modified paginator implementations, the `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra:` branch only runs inside `if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value:`. In that prev-cursor case, `start_offset` is set to `offset` (`start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), so the slice start and the later length comparison are consistent; there isn’t a `start_offset != offset` situation for this branch in the diff.

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap: the entire new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class (~95 lines including novel negative-offset logic) and modified `BasePaginator.get_result` slicing ship with zero tests in this diff; the shared `BasePaginator` regression silently affects every paginated endpoint and pre-existing tests never exercise negative or prev-with-negative offsets

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new pagination logic (new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class with conditional negative-offset slicing in `get_result`) and also changes shared pagination behavior in `BasePaginator.get_result` from `queryset[offset:stop]` to using `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` before slicing. No test files or test updates appear in this diff to cover the new class or the altered slicing behavior, so the concern about a coverage gap for these nontrivial, cross-cutting changes is specific and diff-grounded (even if the claim about what pre-existing tests do/don’t cover can’t be proven from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated on a raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` with no feature flag or way to disable short of a code deploy, and it silently changes the pagination contract — cursor semantics differ between `DateTimePaginator` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, so operators cannot turn the broken path off during an incident and cursor drift between paths produces skipped/duplicated rows

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint now conditionally switches paginator implementations based purely on a raw query param (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) plus an auth check, with no feature-flag/ops kill switch in the diff (only client opt-in/out). That does introduce an operational/contract risk: the same endpoint can emit/consume different cursor behaviors depending on whether `OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator` is used (`paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator`), so if clients toggle the param (or different clients use different paths) cursor compatibility/drift could cause skipped/duplicated rows. The diff doesn’t prove an active production break by itself, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern about controllability and API contract stability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Dead/vestigial design: since the negative-offset branch crashes immediately, the entire 'negative offset support' rationale for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is infeasible in the Django ORM, meaning ~60 lines including the endpoint branch and `enable_advanced_features` plumbing fail the deletion test — maintainers inherit a second parallel paginator code path that adds no reachable optimization

adjudication.rationale: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices (it raises immediately), so the advertised/implemented “negative offset support” path will crash if a negative offset cursor is supplied. The earlier paginator change also keeps `start_offset = offset` for `cursor.is_prev`, which would likewise pass a negative start through. This is a concrete, diff-grounded broken-behavior risk, not just an architecture concern.

That would raise a `NameError` whenever `optimized_pagination=true` is used and `request.user.is_superuser` is false (since the RHS would be evaluated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.offset < 0, and Django's QuerySet raises 'AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported' on any slice with a negative start; the code comment claims Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically, which is false, causing an unhandled 500 on the audit-log endpoint for any admin using optimized_pagination=true with a crafted negative-offset cursor

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is an untested hand-copied clone of OffsetPaginator.get_result with divergences (e.g. trimming uses offset while slice used start_offset, and cursor_value = 0 fallback instead of max(0, cursor.value)) that will only surface as wrong pages/500s in production

In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start (`start_offset = cursor.offset`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New negative-offset slicing in DateTimePaginator.get_result breaks the start_offset >= 0 invariant with no test update, allowing crafted cursors to cause 500s instead of 4xx via Django's ValueError on negative indexing

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BasePaginator.get_result keeps the raw negative offset on the prev path (start_offset = offset if cursor.is_prev), allowing a crafted prev-cursor with negative offset to reach queryset[negative:stop] and raise the 'Negative indexing is not supported' error, a remote-triggerable 500 on the default path

When the audit log endpoint uses this paginator it still paginates with `order_by='-datetime'`, so the paginator key is plausibly the `datetime` field (a `datetime` object), which is not compatible with `math.floor/ceil` and would raise `TypeError`, leading to 500s on optimized requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Negative-offset slicing in the paginator raises Django's `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`, producing a 500 instead of efficient bidirectional pagination (sites: paginator.py:876-882 and paginator.py:184-186)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces paths where a Django QuerySet is sliced with a negative start index. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it does `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Django explicitly rejects negative indexing/slicing on QuerySets (raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`), causing a 500. Additionally, the earlier change in `paginator.py` sets `start_offset = ... if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so a negative `offset` with `cursor.is_prev` can also flow into slicing. This matches the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Clamping forward-cursor negative offsets to 0 in `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` silently returns the wrong page as a 200, and the subsequent `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check uses the unclamped offset so boundary correction can never match

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, the `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` “boundary correction” logic is only executed inside `if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value:`. In that branch, `start_offset` is set to `offset` (no clamping), so there is no mismatch between the slice window and the `offset + limit + extra` comparison. The finding’s claim that clamping causes the boundary correction to “never match” is not supported by the diff. While forward negative offsets are clamped to 0 (`not cursor.is_prev`), the diff does not establish that forward negative offsets are valid/expected, and the cited broken correction path does not apply to forward pagination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new paginator behavior is gated on a raw query param with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled without a code deploy; operators have no kill switch and the two paginators produce different cursor formats for the same endpoint depending on caller permissions

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint now switches pagination behavior based on a raw query param (`request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and caller privileges (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`) with no feature-flag/options-based control shown in the diff. That means operators have no runtime kill switch besides callers omitting the param, and the same endpoint can return different pagination/cursor behavior depending on who calls it (DateTimePaginator vs new OptimizedCursorPaginator), which is an operability/consistency concern rather than a directly verifiable correctness break.

No test files are added/modified anywhere in the diff to cover these behaviors (prev-cursor trimming, datetime key handling via `get_item_key`, negative-offset slicing), so the finding about zero test coverage for the new core behaviors is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Prev-cursor result trimming is dead/incorrect under the new offset regime: `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: results = results[:-1]` compares against the unclamped offset while results were sliced from `start_offset`, so the trim either never fires or fires on the wrong page shape, leaving a duplicated boundary row when paging backwards

adjudication.rationale: The cited trimming block (`if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value: ... elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: ...`) only executes when `cursor.is_prev` is true. In both updated implementations, when `cursor.is_prev` is true, `start_offset` is set to `offset` (i.e., it is not clamped via `max(0, offset)`), so the slice is taken from `queryset[offset: offset + limit + extra]`. Therefore there is no mismatch between `start_offset` used for slicing and the `offset` used in the length comparison, contradicting the finding’s premise that it compares against an “unclamped offset” while slicing from a clamped `start_offset`.
